title: Tupac Murder Trial: Why Keffe D Was Convicted in Under 3 Hours

lines.say: For twenty-seven years, nobody was charged with killing Tupac Shakur.
This summer, it took a jury less than three hours to convict.
The man they convicted is Duane Davis, known as Keffe D.
Prosecutors never said he pulled the trigger. They said he planned the shooting, and supplied the gun.
And the heart of the case, prosecutors said, was his own words.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC INTERVIEW SET, NOT A LIKENESS

lines.say: A police interview in 2008. Television. Even a memoir, in which he told the story himself.
Now he says he only told those stories because he was paid.
On the thirteenth of October, he's due to be sentenced. He faces up to life in prison, without parole.
This is how a thirty-year-old case finally reached a verdict, and what the record still can't tell us.

shots.sub: The case against Duane "Keffe D" Davis

lines.say: Las Vegas. The seventh of September, 1996.
Tupac Shakur had been at a boxing match at the MGM Grand.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC CASINO HOTEL, NOT THE MGM GRAND

lines.say: Prosecutors later told the jury that earlier that night, Tupac, Suge Knight and their group had beaten up Davis's nephew in the hotel.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · NOT THE REAL SECURITY FOOTAGE

rows.text: his nephew was beaten that night

lines.say: His name was Orlando Anderson.
A few hours later, at about a quarter past eleven, Tupac was riding in the passenger seat of a black BMW. Suge Knight, the head of Death Row Records, was driving.
They stopped at a red light, near Flamingo Road and Koval Lane. A white Cadillac pulled up alongside.
Someone inside it opened fire.
Tupac was hit several times. Knight survived, with minor injuries.
Six days later, on the thirteenth of September, Tupac Shakur died at University Medical Center.
Anderson denied any involvement.
In 1998, he died in an unrelated shooting in Compton. He was never charged.
Years went by. Then decades. Nobody was charged.
In 2018, Las Vegas police said it was still an open homicide.
But one man said, again and again, that he'd been there.
Duane Davis. Police and prosecutors said he was a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips.

shots.name: Duane "Keffe D" Davis
lines: A former gang leader, police said

lines.say: In 2008, he sat down with a federal and local task force investigating the killing, led by Los Angeles detective Greg Kading.

lower.title: Greg Kading
lower.kicker: LAPD task force · detective shown is generic

lines.say: It was what's called a proffer, or a 'queen for a day' interview. And Davis told them a story.
He said he was in the front passenger seat of the Cadillac, and that he handed a gun to the men in the back.

shots.title: What Davis told investigators
lines: Gun:    handed to the back seat

lines.say: And he named the man he said fired the shots: his own nephew, Orlando Anderson.
Anderson had denied any involvement, and he was never charged. By then, he had been dead for a decade.
Ten years later, Davis went on television.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC INTERVIEW SET, NOT A LIKENESS

lines.say: He said the shots came from the back seat of the car he was in. But he wouldn't say who fired.

rows.text: Shots from the back seat, he said.

lines.say: His stories didn't always match. In one interview, he said he ducked when the shooting started, and didn't know who had the gun.
Then, in 2019, he published a memoir, Compton Street Legend. In it, he said he was in the Cadillac, and passed the gun into the back seat.

shots.title: Compton Street Legend
lines: The gun: passed to the back seat

lines.say: He never claimed to have fired a shot himself.
In July 2023, Las Vegas police searched a home in Henderson, Nevada, linked to Davis.

shots.label: ILLUSTRATION · GENERIC HOUSE, NOT THE REAL HOME

lines.say: Two months later, on the twenty-ninth of September, police arrested him near his home, while he was out on a walk.
A grand jury had indicted him for murder, with a deadly weapon.
District Attorney Steve Wolfson said: "Today, we are taking that first step."

shots.text: Today we are taking that first step.
shots.who: District Attorney Steve Wolfson, announcing the charge

lines.say: Davis pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors did not seek the death penalty.
He was never released on bail. In 2024, the judge refused to accept bail money put up by a rap manager, finding it hadn't been shown to come from legal sources.
His lawyers argued he'd been promised immunity, back in 2008. The judge found no proof of any immunity deal.
And in July 2026, Judge Carli Kierny ruled that the jury could hear the 2008 interview, and refused to exclude the memoir. She found Davis had adopted the book as his own.
The trial opened in August 2026.
Prosecutors told jurors Davis didn't pull the trigger, but that he planned the shooting, in revenge for his nephew's beating, and supplied the gun.
His defence said he'd made up or embellished his stories, for money and notoriety. That nothing backed them up. That the gun was never found.
His own lawyer told the jury that Davis was, quote, 'full of crap' when he told those stories.

shots.who: Davis's defence, in opening statements, on the stories Davis told

lines.say: Suge Knight, who survived the shooting, was on the prosecution's witness list. He was never called.
Of the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac, Davis is the only one still alive.

shots.label: still alive, of the men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac
shots.note: Davis now says he wasn't there

lines.say: Davis did not testify. His defence rested after calling three witnesses.
In his closing argument, prosecutor Binu Palal said Davis got a gun and 'went hunting'. "It's a plan," he said, "not an impulse."

shots.text: It's a plan, not an impulse.
shots.who: Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal, closing argument, 31 August 2026

lines.say: On the thirty-first of August, 2026, after less than three hours, the jury found Duane Davis guilty of first-degree murder, with a deadly weapon.
Tupac's sister, Sekyiwa Shakur, cried, and hugged the prosecutors. The family said it was elated, and relieved.
The verdict came one week before the thirtieth anniversary of the shooting.

shots.label: since the shooting
shots.note: Anniversary: Sept 7, 2026, one week after the verdict

lines.say: Davis told the judge he wanted to appeal. He'll be able to, once he's sentenced.

And he now says he's innocent. In a jailhouse interview with ABC, he said he only confessed because he was paid. After the verdict, he told The Hollywood Reporter he wasn't even in Las Vegas that night.

rows.text: Says he was paid to talk
Says he wasn't in Las Vegas

lines.say: Three times over the years, he said he was there. Now he says he wasn't.
Davis has been held in the Clark County Detention Center since his arrest.
On the thirteenth of October, 2026, he's due to be sentenced. He faces up to life in prison, without the possibility of parole.
After the verdict, the district attorney said there still isn't enough evidence to charge anyone else.

rows.text: not enough evidence to charge anyone else

lines.say: So, here's where the record stands.
Tupac Shakur was shot in Las Vegas in September 1996, and died six days later.
Duane Davis is the only person ever charged. A jury convicted him of first-degree murder. Prosecutors never said he fired the gun.

shots.title: Duane "Keffe D" Davis
items: 2023 · INDICTED · the only person ever charged
Not accused of firing the shots

lines.say: He says he's innocent, and he plans to appeal. And the man he once named as the shooter, Orlando Anderson, denied any involvement, and was never charged.

lines: He says he is innocent and plans to appeal
